recipes.name: Tampopo Ramen
ingredients: 1 inch large scallion, cut into 6 pieces
4 quarts of water (note: kombu leaves must soak in water for 24 hours)
2 inch knob of ginger, peeled and chopped
For the Noodles (can also be store bought):
1 ounce of vital wheat gluten (about 1/4 cup)
instructions: Soak large kombu leaves in the water for 24 hours. - 4 kombu leaves - 4 quarts of water (note: kombu leaves must soak in water for 24 hours)
Cut nails off of chicken feet. - 1 pound chicken feet

In a large stockpot, add pork spare ribs, chicken wings, chicken feet, garlic, scallion, onion, and kombu water. - 1 pound chicken feet - ¼ pound pork spare ribs - 2 pounds chicken wings - 1 whole head of garlic halved - 1 inch large scallion cut into 6 pieces - 1 whole onion halved
Place over low heat and keep broth below 200°F. Skim any scum off the top of the surface and dispose of it.
After 4 hours, add bonito and dried anchovies. Allow to continue to simmer for 1 hour. - 1 cup bonito - 1 cup dried anchovies
Pour broth through strainer into large glass bowl. Chill overnight.
For the Pork
Preheat oven to 275°F.

In a pan over high heat, sear the pork shoulder but leave the pork belly unseared. Then, place pork shoulder and belly into baking dish. Top with soy sauce, mirin, sake, shallot, ginger, and garlic. - Pork belly and/or pork shoulder - ½ cup soy sauce - 1 cup sake - 1 whole shallot halved - 2 inch knob of ginger peeled and chopped - 6 cloves of garlic crushed - 1 cup mirin
Replace top but leave slightly ajar. Allow pork to braise in oven for about 3 hours until tender and cooked.
For the Tared Sauce

In the pan you used to sear the pork shoulder, saute the dried anchovies over medium heat. Deglaze with soy sauce. Break apart and add kombu leaves. Allow to steep without boiling for about 10 minutes. - ½ cup dried anchovies - 2 cups soy sauce - Several kombu leaves
Add in bonito flake. Allow to steep for an additional 5 minutes. Using a strainer, drain the fishy soy sauce mixture into a glass measuring cup and set aside. - ½ cup bonito flakes
Wipe the pan and place over medium heat. Combine sake, mirin, and brown sugar before bringing the mixture to a boil to cook off the alcohol. - ¼ cup sake - 4 tbsp of mirin - 1 ½ tbsp of brown sugar
Add the fishy soy sauce mixture to the pan. Combine and set aside.
For the Noodles
Preheat oven to 225°F.
On a parchment covered baking sheet, pour out baking soda. Place baking sheet in the oven for about an hour. - 1 cup baking soda

Combine bread flour and vital wheat gluten. In warm water, dissolve the additional baking soda. Pour baking soda mixture into bread flour mixture. Combine until a dough forms. - 8 ½ ounces bread flour (about 2 cups) - 1 ounce of vital wheat gluten (about 1/4 cup) - 1 tbsp of additional baking soda - ½ cup warm water
Knead dough for about 5 minutes. Cover in plastic wrap and allow to rest for an hour.
Roll the dough out using a pasta machine until it can be placed into the pasta cutter. Run the dough through the pasta cutter and then toss with some corn starch.
Place the noodles on a parchment covered baking sheet and cover with plastic wrap. Refrigerate overnight.
For the To Assemble Soup
Boil noodles for no more than 30 seconds. - For the Noodles (can also be store bought):
Place 2 Tbsp of Tare into a bowl. Add a few ladlefuls of the boiling broth, followed by the noodles. - For the Tare Sauce - For the Broth

Slice the pork and place on top. Garnish with a kamaboko, scallions, menma, and nori. - Kamaboko (Japanese fish cake) - Chopped scallions - Menma (braised bamboo shoots) - 1 sheet of nori (dried seaweed) - For the Pork
Slurp your noodles.
